title: Orange-Based Ethiopian Kid-Friendly Injera
description: A lacto-vegetarian-friendly, molten, kid-friendly ethiopian dish featuring oranges and flambe, served as a traditional injera flatbread.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.notes: adds sweetness and complexity to the injera

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: for greasing the pan and flame caramelization

instructions: Mix together teff flour, sugar, and yeast in a large bowl.
Gradually add in water, stirring with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms a smooth batter.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let it ferment in a warm, draft-free place for 24 hours.
Preheat a large non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat, greasing it with unsalted butter.
Pour 1/4 cup of the batter into the skillet and tilt it to evenly coat the bottom.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.
Use a spatula to carefully loosen the injera from the skillet and flip it over.
Cook for an additional 30-45 seconds, until the other side is lightly browned and crispy.
Repeat with the remaining batter, adjusting the heat as needed to prevent burning.

To flambe, carefully pour a small amount of orange juice into the skillet, followed by a few pieces of sugar. The mixture should bubble and slightly brown. Use a spatula to carefully lift the edges of the injera and tilt the skillet to allow the flame to spread evenly.
Cook for an additional 30 seconds to 1 minute, until the caramelized sugar and citrus flavors have infused into the injera.
Serve hot, garnished with additional orange zest if desired.
Allow the injera to cool completely before storing in an airtight container for up to 3 days.
